title: U.S. House · Texas's 28th Congressional District
area: South Texas along the border, from Laredo (Webb County) north toward San Antonio.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections. Ballotpedia identifies this race as a battleground: during redistricting, the district was redrawn to one Donald Trump would have carried 54.8%-44.4% in 2024, compared to 53.1%-45.8% under the prior lines, making it one of 23 Democratic-held U.S. House seats up in 2026 that Trump won in 2024.

Henry Cuellar was indicted in May 2024 on federal charges of bribery, unlawful foreign influence, and money laundering, alleging that he and his wife accepted $600,000 from an Azerbaijan-linked oil-and-gas company and a Mexican bank; House Democratic rules required him to leave his Appropriations subcommittee post after the indictment. President Trump pardoned Cuellar and his wife in December 2025, and Cuellar retook the subcommittee leadership position; the Cook Political Report subsequently moved its rating of the race from Toss-up to Lean Democratic.

In the March 3, 2026 primaries, Cuellar defeated Ricardo Villarreal and Andrew Vantine 58.1% to 37.0% to 5.0% for the Democratic nomination, and Tano Tijerina defeated Eileen Day 74.3% to 25.7% for the Republican nomination. Marlon Duran advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 convention.

summary.text: Henry Cuellar is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 28th District, a former state legislator and Texas Secretary of State who was indicted on federal bribery charges in 2024 and pardoned by President Trump in December 2025.

background.text: Born in Laredo, Texas, in 1955; earned an associate degree from Laredo Community College, a bachelor's in foreign service from Georgetown University, a J.D. from the University of Texas at Austin, a master's in international trade from Texas A&M International University, and a Ph.D. in government from UT Austin.
Served in the Texas House of Representatives from 1987 to 2001 and as Texas Secretary of State in 2001.

record.text: Was indicted in May 2024 on federal charges of bribery, unlawful foreign influence, and money laundering; House Democratic rules required him to leave his House Appropriations Homeland Security subcommittee leadership post after the indictment.
Was pardoned by President Trump in December 2025 and retook his leadership position on the Appropriations Homeland Security subcommittee.

Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including as Ranking Member of its Homeland Security subcommittee and as a member of its Military Construction-Veterans Affairs and Defense subcommittees.

candidates.name: Tano Tijerina
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 74.3% of the vote

summary.text: Tano Tijerina is the former Webb County Judge, a rancher and former minor league baseball player who won the Republican nomination to challenge Rep. Henry Cuellar.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in fitness and sports from Texas A&M International University; played minor league baseball and worked in ranching.
Served as Webb County Judge, winning re-election in the 2018 Democratic primary for that office before later running for Congress as a Republican.

priorities.text: His campaign website lists border security and immigration enforcement, lowering taxes and cutting federal regulation, and supporting cryptocurrency innovation among his priorities.

positions.summary: Says the border must be secured, the law enforced, and illegal crossings stopped, while backing a practical, bipartisan path for immigrants who came 'the right way.'
Says he would fight to lower taxes for working families and small businesses and cut federal regulations, citing his record lowering property taxes five times in ten years as Webb County Judge.

record.text: As Webb County Judge, lowered property taxes five times over ten years, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Marlon Duran
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 state convention

summary.text: Marlon Duran is the Green Party nominee in this race; little public biographical or policy information is available.
